transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-08-22
Start time: 15:00 PT
Duration: 47m
Attendees: Alex Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), Jade Morris (Redwood SE), Marta Lopez (CTO, SynapseAI), Derrick Huang (Head of ML), Evan Smith (Platform Eng), Sana Rizvi (Security)

Summary: Short discovery focused on integration patterns for SynapseAI's platform. Main topics: SDK usage, LangChain/LlamaIndex footprints, gateway/proxy insertion, rate limiting/quotas, and observability hooks for production rollout. Customer is evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private deployment options; strong security/residency needs mentioned.

Topics: Integration SDKs, LangChain/LlamaIndex, gateway/proxy, rate limits/quotas, observability, private/VPC options, KMS/SOC2

Action items (recap at end): see action_items field

Transcript body:
[00:00] Alex Kim: Hey everyone, Alex from Redwood here. Thanks for carving out time, we'll keep this tight, about 45 minutes. Who should I look to for architecture decisions from Synapse?
[00:18] Marta Lopez: Hi Alex -- Marta here. I'll be making the call with input from Derrick and Evan. We'll want the SE detail on how this hooks into our existing LangChain pipelines.
[00:29] Priya Patel: Great, thanks Marta. Quick agenda from our side: understand your current integration patterns, talk about SDKs and gateways, go over rate limiting and quotas, and then discuss security and private options. Sound okay?
[00:42] Derrick Huang: Yeah that sounds right. We're running a mix of LangChain and a few homegrown orchestrators. Mostly LlamaIndex in our RAG flows, and some direct SDK calls for chat features.
[00:56] Evan Smith: Platform note: we usually front outbound AI calls with our gateway/proxy layer for routing and auth, and it enforces our own rate limits. We want to know how Redwood fits in there without tearing up that stack.
[01:10] Alex Kim: Perfect. Quick boolean — are you exploring hosted first or looking weight toward dedicated/private?
[01:18] Marta Lopez: We want a POC on hosted to validate latency/cost, but enterprise requires private (VPC) or dedicated in the medium term for data residency and audit controls. Security will drive the procurement.
[01:30] Sana Rizvi: Yep SOC 2 + KMS integration are musts. Also need clarity on audit logs and RBAC for team separation.
[01:38] Priya Patel: Understood. We have hosted for quick dev POCs, Redwood Dedicated for reserved GPU pools, and Redwood Private for VPC/on-prem. For KMS we integrate with customer KMS/HSM; we also surface audit logs to the customer's syslog or S3 depending on the deployment.
[01:55] Marta Lopez: Good. Let's dive into SDKs: we're on Python and Node; LangChain is a big part of our stack. Do you provide first-class LangChain helpers or do we use the generic SDK?
[02:08] Priya Patel: We have official SDKs in both Python and Node with helpers for streaming and function/tool calling. For LangChain specifically, we maintain adapters — e.g., a Redwood LLM wrapper that plugs into LangChain's LLM interface, and we've seen customers use LlamaIndex with Redwood through LangChain adapters as well. There are example notebooks.
[02:27] Derrick Huang: Any gotchas with LlamaIndex? We've seen tokenization and context window issues with big indexes. Also curious about caching — does Redwood do prefix cache / KV cash across requests?
[02:41] Alex Kim: (laughs) KV cash yes — KV cache. We support KV cache and prefix caching that can be configured per-model. It helps with repeated context patterns, reduces cost and latency but it's configurable because you may not want cached PII.
[02:56] Priya Patel: To add, our SDK exposes cache-control headers and a cache policy object so your orchestrator can decide what gets cached. For LlamaIndex integrations we recommend controlling cache at the chain level.
[03:10] Evan Smith: How about gateway insertion? We already have an internal proxy that does auth, observability hooks, and some transformations. Can Redwood live behind a gateway and still do streaming and function-calls?
[03:21] Jade Morris: Absolutely. We support both proxied traffic — you can route through your gateway to the Redwood API endpoint — and we also provide a gateway pattern where Redwood's edge can talk to a customer proxy for on-prem controls. For streaming, WebSocket and chunked HTTP are supported; function-calling metadata flows through. Sometimes customers do token exchange at the gateway level.
[03:40] Marta Lopez: Any limitations on embedding sizes or concurrency that would impact our RAG at scale? Our embedding pipeline is heavy — multiple models and high QPS.
[03:51] Priya Patel: For embeddings, we recommend batching and dedicated capacity if you need predictable throughput. Hosted has soft quotas that we can increase; dedicated gives you reserved throughput. Concurrency limits depend on model size and GPU config; we can share model performance profiles.
[04:10] Derrick Huang: Rate limits — we have complex quotas per-team. Can we enforce quotas per API key and implement burst policies? We don't want to put everything on one tenant-level limit.
[04:20] Alex Kim: Yes, Redwood supports token- and request-level quotas per API key and per route. You can set burst windows and throttling policies. On Dedicated/Private you can run the rate limiter inside your VPC or use our control plane to push policies.
[04:35] Evan Smith: Observability: what hooks do you provide? We need per-request tracing, token cost breakdowns, and ability to wire into Grafana/Prometheus and our internal SLO tooling.
[04:46] Priya Patel: We emit structured logs with request IDs, token counts, latencies, model used. There's a tracing header we propagate so you can correlate with your traces. We have integrations for Prometheus metrics and an API to stream metrics to your monitoring. The Console surfaces cost breakdown per API key and per-route.
[05:05] Marta Lopez: How invasive is the instrumentation? We want minimal code changes in LangChain chains.
[05:11] Jade Morris: Minimal — the adapters do the heavy lifting; you wrap the LLM client and you get streaming and the tracing header automatically. For deeper telemetry you can add a small middleware to push events to your telemetry collector.
[05:25] Derrick Huang: On the SDK surface, do you have retry semantics or idempotency for calls? We have background workers that retry and we need determinism for function calls.
[05:35] Priya Patel: Our client includes configurable retry/backoff policies, idempotency tokens support for requests where needed, and guidance for function-calling idempotency patterns. For background jobs we usually recommend deterministic prompts or an external job tracker.
[05:53] Evan Smith: Latency numbers — can you share typical 95th percentile for a 4k-context chat on hosted?
[06:00] Alex Kim: We can share benchmark pdfs but ballpark: for a medium-sized open model on hosted you might see 95th ~300-500ms per token depending on batching and KV cache patterns; for dedicated with pinned GPU you'd likely see lower and more consistent tails. We'll send the benchmark spreadsheet.
[06:18] Marta Lopez: Please send. We'll compare to our internal SLOs.
[06:24] Sana Rizvi: Quick security question — if we choose Private, how does the control plane work? Is there a separate plane in AWS, or is it fully customer-controlled?
[06:33] Priya Patel: In Private deployment we ship a customer-managed control plane component that talks to a lightweight Redwood control service only for licensing and health — you can restrict it to your VPC or run it air-gapped with manual updates. KMS integration uses customer KMS keys and we don't store plaintext model inputs in our control plane.
[06:52] Derek (mislabelled): [crosstalk] we saw a note about audit logs to S3. Is that push or pull?
[06:58] Alex Kim: We push logs to your S3/Cloud Storage or forward to syslog; options for streaming or daily rollups. We also support SIEM integrations.
[07:10] Derrick Huang: For the LangChain flows — do you recommend running LlamaIndex within our infra and call Redwood for generation only, or is it better to host the embedding/indexing with Redwood?
[07:23] Priya Patel: Most customers keep indexing in their infra because indexing/storage often ties to business data. They use Redwood for embeddings and generation. But if you want to offload, we can support embeddings as a service; you'd want to consider network egress and residency.
[07:39] Evan Smith: Cost control concern. Our main objective is to keep per-request cost predictable. Do you offer token budget alarms and per-route spend controls?
[07:48] Jade Morris: Yes, the console has token/budget alerts and route-level spend caps; you can also set programmatic throttles via the API. During pilot we recommend a spend cap to avoid surprises.
[08:02] Marta Lopez: On the topic of SDKs — we sometimes use LlamaIndex directly without LangChain. Is there a recommended pattern?
[08:10] Priya Patel: LlamaIndex can call our SDK directly; for many teams the easiest path is to use a thin adapter that maps LlamaIndex's calls to the Redwood client. We have examples in the repo.
[08:22] Derrick Huang: Any quirks with function-calling through the LangChain wrappers? We use function calling for structured outputs and downstream processors rely on exact JSON shapes.
[08:34] Priya Patel: We pass function calls and structured outputs through; our SDK validates and preserves the JSON payload. There is a caveat: streaming function outputs come as events and you need to reassembly them, but our wrapper supports that reassembly.
[08:50] Evan Smith: About quotas again — if we go dedicated, can we partition GPU pools per team and enforce different quotas?
[08:59] Alex Kim: Yes, Dedicated supports logical pools and capacity reservation per pool. You can set policies per pool, and the console shows utilization per pool.
[09:08] Marta Lopez: What about canary rollouts and model versioning? We need to test new model revisions against a holdout prompt set before full rollout.
[09:17] Jade Morris: We have rollout primitives: canary, A/B, and automatic fallback. You can pin routes to model versions and schedule gradual rollouts tied to evaluation metrics. There's built-in eval hooks so you can run prompt sets and alert on regressions.
[09:31] Derrick Huang: For our pilot we'd like to test with LangChain chains for 2 weeks and check quality and cost. Does Redwood provide evaluation tooling or do we bring our own?
[09:40] Priya Patel: Redwood Optimize has quality monitoring and regression alerts tied to prompt sets — you can upload your evals and we'll surface drift. For pilot we can provision an eval workspace.
[09:53] Marta Lopez: Great. A few integration nitty-gritty things: is there an SDK proxy mode so we can run a local sidecar that forwards to Redwood but injects our auth and headers? That would be ideal.
[10:06] Alex Kim: Yes, many customers run a sidecar or edge proxy that handles auth and telemetry. We also provide a lightweight gateway image if you want a supported sidecar. It handles token exchange and header mapping.
[10:20] Evan Smith: Any constraints on TLS mutual auth or cert pinning when using the sidecar?
[10:27] Priya Patel: We support mTLS and cert pinning in Private deployments; for hosted you can use token exchange and TLS. mTLS is available in Dedicated/Private for stricter requirements.
[10:38] Derrick Huang: Ok one more technical: how does Redwood handle prefix/long-context KV caching with LlamaIndex? We're worried about cache staleness for dynamic content.
[10:50] Jade Morris: Cache staleness is solved by TTLs and cache invalidation hooks. You can set per-key TTLs or push explicit invalidation calls. For LlamaIndex you can tie invalidation to index updates.
[11:03] Marta Lopez: Are there example configs you can share for LangChain/LlamaIndex + gateway?
[11:08] Priya Patel: Yes, we have a repo with three patterns: direct SDK, LangChain adapter, and sidecar gateway. I'll share links after the call.
[11:17] Alex Kim: (shares link) https://redwood.ai/examples/langchain-lamaindex-patterns — note: transcription may spell that weirdly in auto notes.
[11:28] Sana Rizvi: On compliance — can audit logs include raw prompt text or do you recommend redaction? We have PHI in some flows.
[11:36] Priya Patel: We recommend redaction for PHI. Logs can be configured to include hashed IDs instead of raw prompts. In Private deployments you can choose to not export raw prompts from the runtime.
[11:48] Evan Smith: Regarding billing and quotas during pilot — can we cap spend and get notified? We don't want a runaway spend.
[11:56] Alex Kim: Absolutely — spend caps and alerts are standard for pilots. We'll configure an initial cap and raise as you validate.
[12:05] Derrick Huang: For the pilot we'll likely use a small set of real user prompts and a synthetic higher QPS profile to stress-test quotas. Is there a sandbox or load driver you recommend?
[12:16] Priya Patel: We have an internal load harness and can provide a simple k6 or locust script. We also share a benchmark spreadsheet with model p50/p95/token rates.
[12:29] Marta Lopez: Please share the harness and benchmarks.
[12:33] Jade Morris: Will do.
[12:36] Alex Kim: Switching back to observability: do you provide per-token latency breakdowns? We want to see where time is spent (queue, decode, network).
[12:45] Priya Patel: Yes, we provide breakdowns in the Console: queue time, kernel exec time, decode time, and network. These are surfaced per-request and aggregated.
[12:57] Evan Smith: Good. For our internal gateway we plan to set route-level timeouts. Any gotchas for streaming endpoints if gateway closes connection early?
[13:07] Jade Morris: If gateway closes early you may get partial streams; we provide a final status event so you can detect partial completions. We also support resumable streaming for some models.
[13:19] Derrick Huang: Let's talk about model variants for cost/latency tradeoffs. Can we set fallback policies so if premium model is down or expensive we fallback to a cheaper model?
[13:31] Alex Kim: Yes, smart routing lets you set policy rules: region, latency, cost, model family. You can have automatic fallback to a cheaper or quantized model when latency spikes or capacity is low.
[13:44] Marta Lopez: For enterprise controls — can we restrict which teams can deploy model updates? Need RBAC and approvals.
[13:51] Priya Patel: Console has RBAC and approval flows; you can require code owner or security approval before a rollout and tie deployment to an audit ticket.
[14:04] Marta Lopez: Any limitations on supported models for Private/on-prem? We plan to bring an open model we fine-tuned internally.
[14:12] Alex Kim: You can bring custom models, but we validate compatibility with the runtime and provide quantization/compilation guidance. Some experimental ops may need a supported kernel. We'll run an onboarding test.
[14:25] Evan Smith: Do you handle model hosting for us if we bring a large fine-tuned model? Disk, sharding, etc?
[14:34] Priya Patel: For Dedicated we can host and manage model files if you prefer; in Private we can help with the on-prem packaging or you can self-host the model artifacts. There are recommended storage/sharding configs in the doc.
[14:48] Derrick Huang: One last item — is there an option to run a local emulator of Redwood for dev so devs aren't hitting hosted infra?
[14:57] Jade Morris: We have a dev-client and a limited local runtime for offline devs - it's not full-performance but useful for integration testing.
[15:06] Marta Lopez: Okay let's recap next steps.
[15:09] Alex Kim: Recap: we'll send dedicated pricing and private deployment checklist, benchmarks and the LangChain/LlamaIndex example repo, a load harness, and SOC2/KMS notes. Priya will run a perf test on a small prompt set, and we'll schedule a SE deep-dive to test gateway insertion and rate-limit configs.
[15:28] Sana Rizvi: We'll send sample prompts and traffic profile by Monday.
[15:32] Alex Kim: Great. Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with links and a calendar invite for the deep-dive.
[15:40] End of meeting.
